div.head: I Cn 20.2
div.ab: ⁊ eac ah hlaforda gehwylc þæs formycle þearfe, þæt he his men rihtlice healde.
And eac ah hlaforda gehwylc þæs formicele þearfe, þæt he his menn rihtlice heolde.
⁊ eac ah laforda gehwylc ðæs formyccle ðearfe, þæt he his men rihtlice healde.
Et unicuique domino magnum opus est, ut hominem suum recte deducat.
⁊ eac ah laforda gehwylc ðæs formyccle ðearfe þæt he his men rihtlice healde.
And eac ah hlaforda gehwylc þæs formycle þearfe þæt he his men rihtlice healde.
Und auch jeder der Herren hat dazu gar starke Verpflichtung, dass er seine Untergebenen rechtlich halte.
And also every lord has very great need to treat his men rightly.
And likewise it is the great duty of every lord to treat his men justly.
And also every lord has very great benefit from treating his men justly.
And likewise the principal obligation of every lord is to treat his people justly.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
